summary: The macOS credential store of both ports: /usr/bin/security in interactive mode, commands on standard input, one login keychain item per service. Items are created by the security tool itself, so every build of either port reads them without a keychain prompt.

operations.get: probe; absent -> absent. read; absent -> absent. When the probe did not show ownedMarker and the value (trimmed) matches tokenPattern, migrate with that value and ignore the migration's outcome. The value is returned trimmed and otherwise unchanged; callers validate it.
operations.set: a token that does not match tokenPattern is SERVICE_PROTOCOL_INVALID and nothing is spawned. remove (absent is fine), then add.

denied: user name or passphrase you entered is not correct
classification.rule: Markers are searched in standard error, in this order. Without a marker, a non-zero exit status is unavailable and exit 0 is ok. A spawn failure, a signal, the time bound or an output stream over outputLimitBytes is unavailable.

outcomes.absent: get: no key (signed out); delete: success; add: unavailable
outcomes.interaction-not-allowed: CREDENTIAL_STORE_UNAVAILABLE with the keychain-access reason and action
outcomes.cancelled: kill the tool; CANCELLED, except while set runs: CREDENTIAL_STORE_UNAVAILABLE with the outcome-unknown reason

keychain-access.reason: the macOS keychain needs approval in a prompt before this build can read the stored key (the key was saved by an earlier build of the CLI); set {variable} for this command
keychain-access.action: Run the command in a desktop session and allow access in the macOS keychain prompt once, or set {variable} for this command.

outcome-unknown.reason: the command was cancelled before the operating system credential store confirmed the change, so it is unknown whether the key was stored; set {variable} for this command
outcome-unknown.action: Set {variable} for this command, or unlock or configure the operating system credential store, then retry.
